messages.content: Calculate the probability of getting a head when flipping a coin.

message.content:
For a fair coin (i.e., one that has an equal chance of landing on either side), the probability of obtaining a head on a single flip is:

\[
P(\text{Head}) = \frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total possible outcomes}} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5 \;\text{(or 50 %)}.
\]

If the coin were known to be biased, you would need the specific bias value (e.g., \(p\) for heads) to compute the probability.
